A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CreDRO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CreDRO experiments on OOD detection, corrupted images, computational runtime, and Camelyon17 selective classification, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds label-noise experiments, interpolation comparisons, and further credal-set diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same top-loss batch training and uniform member-specific interpolation, followed by the same box-credal predictions and uncertainty calculations. The CVaR formalization and experimental variants do not replace the proposed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds CIFAR10 training scenarios with 10% and 20% symmetric label noise and clean test data. The existing OOD datasets, image-corruption benchmarks, and Camelyon17 task remain. Regression is still only a proposed extension.

E2.justification: v3 introduces and evaluates CreRAM, a random sample-upweighting control, in the noisy-label comparisons in Tables 6 and 9. Comparator membership in the original experiments is retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include five-member noisy-label experiments, squared and square-root interpolation grids, and FPR@95TPR, mean ID uncertainty, and normalized uncertainty-gap measurements. These extend the existing evaluation framework; the original splits, backbones, training budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic coverage: Section 4.5 tests label-noise vulnerability and loss-guided versus random selection, Appendix D tests interpolation sensitivity, and Appendix F examines whether box-credal gains accompany excessive ID uncertainty. The earlier ensemble-size, hyperparameter, corruption, and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained, including three-run comparisons, Figure 4's stated 15-run averaging, and five medical-experiment runs. New tables extend the existing reporting convention without introducing new statistical tests, confidence intervals, or changed run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 6, 9, 11, and 13–15 add substantial results; matched original tables remain numerically unchanged. At 20% label noise, Table 6 reports SVHN AUROC of 88.9±1.8 for CreDRO versus 83.8±1.0 for CreRAM, but FMNIST favors CreDE, 93.3±0.7 versus 89.8±0.9. These are newly evaluated conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit CVaR weight set, its nesting property, and a top-loss optimization derivation in Equations 6–7, formalizing v1's heuristic explanation. Existing complexity and regression mathematics remain. The claimed exact solution needs an integrality qualification or residual weight when δN is noninteger.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: CreDRO captures disagreement associated with potential distribution shifts and improves OOD detection and medical selective classification. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 proposes a new explanation contrasting persistent minority-group losses with erratic noisy-label losses, motivates uniform interpolation, and clarifies that box and convex-hull representations share identical mean-based accuracy and calibration. The original limitations and regression qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future public code release; v3 supplies a repository link and states that implementation code is publicly available in Section 4 and Appendix B. Existing optimizer, hardware, training, preprocessing, and entropy-computation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Levy et al. (2020) to support the CVaR connection and removes Manchingal et al.'s unified evaluation framework citation. The main research positioning remains. Changes to the Wang survey and credal-distillation references concern the same works with updated bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative order are retained. Local changes expand Sections 3.1 and 4.4, insert the label-noise subsection and two appendix sections, and add conflict-of-interest and impact statements. This is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, changes author and header presentation, and extensively resizes and relocates tables and figures. Six new tables present the added analyses. Figures 1–12 retain their underlying content while being repacked into the new layout.

improvement.justification: The new controls and diagnostics in Section 4.5 and Appendices D and F address previously untested concerns about loss-based selection, interpolation, and box-set conservatism; documented code access also improves reproducibility information. These provide a limited net gain. The label-noise mechanism remains untested directly, the new CVaR equality omits noninteger δN handling, and noisy-label results include exceptions to the retained broad superiority claim.
